chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his brother Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah necessitated upon the women, regarding the Wudu for the Salat, that they should begin with the inside of their arms, and regarding the men, with the back of the arm.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in wiping the arms for men and women during Wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights a key point of jurisprudential divergence (ikhtilaf) between the Ja'fari and Sunni schools regarding the extent of wiping (masah) on the forearms during ablution. While Sunni jurisprudence generally mandates wiping the entire forearm, this narration specifies a distinction based on gender, reflecting the Shia interpretation of the Quranic command to 'wipe' rather than 'wash' the arms. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the specific linguistic nuances of the Quranic verse 5:6 in deriving ritual law.
